chunks: As for the right of the possessor of authority (sultan),

is that you know that you have been made a trial for him, and that he is being tested through you by the authority God has given him over you. And it is upon you not to expose yourself to his displeasure, thereby casting yourself by your own hands into destruction, and becoming his partner in the evil that comes to you from him.

key_terms.السُّلْطَانِ: The possessor of authority, ruler, or leader

ai.seo_question: What is the right of the ruler (sultan) over the individual according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Zayn al-Abidin frames the ruler not merely as an authority figure but as a fellow subject of divine trial (mubtalan), where the individual’s duty is to avoid exposing themselves to the ruler’s wrath to prevent becoming complicit in his misdeeds. This reflects the Shia concept of political quietism and prudence (hilm) during periods of governance, emphasizing that avoiding the ruler's displeasure safeguards the individual from sharing in the 'evil' or sins that may befall the leader. The warning against 'throwing oneself into destruction' underscores the practical necessity of maintaining social stability and personal spiritual safety under earthly authority.
